newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Surveillance names Briton Lilley as new CFO.
newsitem.headline: Surveillance names Briton Lilley as new CFO.

text.p: Swiss inspection and testing group Societe Generale de Surveillance Holding SA said its board had named Paul Anthony Lilley as chief financial officer, replacing Serge Pahud from January.
Lilley, a 38-year-old Briton, joined BET Plc in 1992 and was director of group finance and control on its take-over by Rentokil Initial Plc earlier this year, it added.

Pahud, who is on SGS's executive board, will have responsibility for the quality certification and consultancy business sector. He has responsibilities for the SGS in Britain, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Finland and Scandinavia.
Surveillance chairwoman Elisabeth Salina-Amorini said the change had come at the request of Pahud, a 52-year-old Frenchman who joined SGS in 1973. He has served 16 years as CFO.
"For some time now he had expressed the wish to reorient his career towards the operations side," she told Reuters.
"It is a personal decision," Salina-Amorini added.
She noted that Pahud would retain responsibility for SGS business throughout Europe, except for Germany and the Benelux. He would also oversee quality certification worldwide.

SGS, the world leader in inspections and testing, reported last month that first half group net profit rose by 10.9 per cent and said it expected the positive trend to continue, barring any major foreign exchange deterioration.
Europe represented 42.9 per cent of SGS revenues in 1995.
